name: TX-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +18 partisan lean
Colin Allred's large fundraising advantage ($7.4M raised)
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~98%
Open seat, but the seat's partisan fundamentals dominate
model.rationale: The district's +18 Democratic lean and a favorable national environment point to a comfortable Democratic hold, and markets price a Democratic win near 98%. Allred's substantial fundraising against a little-known, underfunded Republican reinforces a Safe D rating despite the open seat.
model.watch: A major polling surprise or an unexpectedly competitive Allred underperformance against the district's lean would be the main signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jasmine Crockett (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jasmine Crockett's retirement leaves this Dallas-area seat open, but the district's strong Democratic lean of +18 makes it very difficult for Republicans to flip. Democrats nominated Colin Allred, a well-known former congressman and Senate candidate who has raised about $7.4 million, while Republican Patrick Gillespie has reported little fundraising and minimal outside support.

Prediction markets put Democratic chances near 98 percent, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no general-election polling available, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, which point to a Democratic win by roughly 24 points.
